mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of >2% YoY decline in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% month-over-month jointly signal accelerating labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month +0.5% AND PAYEMS < previous month -0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises >0.5% and PAYEMS falls >0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST rises above its 12-month MA by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals a deflationary easing cycle, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < previous month -0.3% AND CPIAUCSL < previous month -0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decline by >0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 8% for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when RSAFS is above its 12-month MA by more than 8% for three consecutive months.
